parts.label: a
parts.description: Write z = -1 + i*sqrt(3) in the form r(cos theta + i sin theta) and in the form r e^(i theta), with -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2 cis(2pi/3) as the modulus-argument form. The argument must lie in -pi < theta <= pi; 2pi/3 only. Exact values only.
parts.notes: A1 for a correct modulus AND a correct argument, by any method (reference angle plus quadrant, or arctan with quadrant resolved). An argument whose quadrant is unresolved, such as +/- pi/3, earns no mark. A1 for both requested forms written correctly with the candidate's r and theta.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write w = 2 - 2i in the form r(cos theta + i sin theta) and in the form r e^(i theta), with -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept sqrt(8) for 2 sqrt(2). An argument of 7pi/4 is outside the stated range and earns no mark.
parts.notes: A1 for a correct modulus AND a correct argument in the required range. A1 for both requested forms written correctly with the candidate's r and theta.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Hence find zw and z/w in the form r e^(i theta), with -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 1/sqrt(2) or 2/(2 sqrt 2) for sqrt(2)/2, and any equivalent exact modulus. Accept cis form alongside the exponential form. Arguments must be in -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.notes: A1 for zw and A1 for z/w; the marks are independent. Each mark is for correct use of the modulus and argument rules (moduli multiplied or divided, arguments added or subtracted), however the working is laid out.
parts.follow_through: Award each A1 for a product or quotient formed correctly by the modulus and argument rules from the candidate's own r and theta in (a) and (b).

parts.label: d
parts.description: Plot and label the points representing z, w and zw on the supplied Argand grid.
parts.tolerance: Accept plotting accurate to about half a grid square. Labels may be z, w, zw or the equivalent coordinates.
parts.notes: A1 for z and w both plotted and labelled correctly. A1 for zw plotted in a position consistent with a modulus of about 5.7 and an argument of about 75 degrees.
parts.follow_through: Award the second A1 for zw plotted consistently with the candidate's own answer to (c).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Use de Moivre's theorem to find the exact value of (1 + i)^8.
parts.tolerance: Accept 16 written as 16 + 0i. Exact value only.
parts.notes: M1 for writing 1 + i in polar or Euler form with a correct modulus and argument (sqrt(2), pi/4). A1 for applying de Moivre's theorem with both the modulus and the argument raised correctly, however the power is written. A1 for the value 16. Repeated squaring ((1 + i)^2 = 2i, then (2i)^4 = 16) is a correct alternative and earns all three marks; note in feedback that de Moivre's theorem was the requested method rather than withholding a mark.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the three cube roots of 8i in the form r e^(i theta), r > 0 and -pi < theta <= pi.
parts.tolerance: The exponential form is required. 2 e^(i 3pi/2) must be converted to 2 e^(-i pi/2) to satisfy the stated range. Cartesian equivalents (sqrt(3) + i, -sqrt(3) + i, -2i) may accompany the answer but do not replace the required form. Accept 2 cis theta only if the exponential form also appears.
parts.notes: M1 for writing 8i in polar or Euler form with the 2k*pi (or equivalent multiple-root) allowance shown or used. A1 for the modulus 2 together with any one correct argument. A1 for the remaining two roots, each with an argument in the required range. A candidate who gives only one root earns at most M1A1.

parts.label: c
parts.description: State the geometric relationship between the three cube roots of 8i on an Argand diagram.

expected.answer: They lie on a circle of radius 2 centred at the origin, equally spaced 2pi/3 apart (vertices of an equilateral triangle).

parts.tolerance: Accept 120 degrees for 2pi/3, and 'equilateral triangle' in place of the spacing statement.
parts.notes: R1 for a statement carrying both the equal-modulus idea (same distance from the origin / on a circle of radius 2) and the equal-spacing idea (equilateral triangle, or arguments differing by 2pi/3). 'They are equally spaced' with no mention of a common modulus or circle earns no mark.
parts.follow_through: Award R1 for a correct description of the candidate's own three roots from (b).
